newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary PM says energy price rise justified.
newsitem.headline: Hungary PM says energy price rise justified.

text.p: Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn said on Friday his government's decision to boost electric and gas prices as of January was justified by costs and was fair to investors.
Electricity rates in Hungary will rise by 24.9 percent and gas prices by 18.8 percent.

"I can safely say that our decision taken yesterday means that for the first time in Hungary, prices will be proportional to costs with respect to energy and fuels and at the same time, those in the energy sector will be able to make a profit," Horn said at an economic forum.
At the same forum for businessmen and diplomats, Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said the price hikes should reassure investors that Hungary honoured its promises.

Some of the private companies which invested in Hungary's utility sector were outraged when the government balked in October at raising utility rates. Investors say the increases are needed to provide a reasonable return on their investment.
"I think the major obstacles have been removed in this field," Medgyessy said.
